comments.text: one thing I wonder about is giving space for script building. so like with sdlc we have a lib/ I think that is where sdlc source lives then gets compiled

replies.text:
Good catch, and it is bigger than lib/. I checked solutions/ontological/agent-pants.yaml in the dev repo: the sdlc plugin ships ~25 build.assets entries from outside the vault (cli/sdlc, the bundled cli/sdlc.js and its wasm, dashboard-spa/dist, conventions/, lib/model/entities, lib/services/docs/*.eta ...) to arbitrary pack paths. v2 as written (containment to marketplaces/<m>, only scripts/ references/ assets/, build.assets dropped by D4) cannot build it.

Proposal, keeping v2 simple:
1. A plugin (and a skill) may hold a src/ folder that never ships, like docs/ and tests/. Script sources live there, or anywhere outside the vault.
2. skillwright does not run builds. Your own build step (bun build, moon task) writes its output into the plugin's scripts/, references/ or assets/ before skillwright build, and those built files are committed or generated in CI.
3. Pack paths follow the three folders: cli/sdlc becomes scripts/sdlc, lib/services/docs/*.eta becomes assets/..., and sdlc's runtime path lookups and the skills' plugin-root paths change to match.

The alternative is keeping a narrow build.assets (from a path outside the vault into one of the three folders). That fits sdlc without moving its source, but it reopens containment. I'd take the src/ + external build route. Which do you want?

ok - so we allow a src folder in a plugin and in a skill? 

should we allow specification of build steps in skillwright.md so a user can just run the skillwright step and it will build it's dist first?

Yes: a src/ folder in a plugin and in a skill, never shipped and never linkable, like docs/ and tests/.

On build steps in skillwright.md (say build.before: [commands], run from the root before the build): it's convenient, but it has costs:
- check must not write to the source tree, yet the steps write into scripts/ and assets/. So check would either skip them (and then compare against stale output) or start writing.
- Running check on a vault you cloned would run its shell commands.
- skillwright would own shell, platform and error handling for other tools.

I'd leave it out of v2: your task runner (moon, just, an npm script) runs the build and then skillwright build. I'd add it as a backlog item for later, with build only, never check. OK with that, or do you want it in v2?
ok

In the spec now: src/ in plugins and skills (never ships, never linkable; listed in the folder table and the never-ship list); new section 3 rule 15, skillwright runs no builds, with a diagram of src/cli.ts built to scripts/tool.js and called as ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js; build steps in skillwright.md added to the Later note and filed as #151; D4 and the impact doc name the sdlc plugin as a consumer that moves to this pattern.

selector.exact: The syntax decides what a token is, not its target. /[[x]] is a call (rule 8). ![[x]] is an embed (section 5). Any other [[x]], and a relative Markdown link, is an ordinary link. An embed resolves by the same rules as a link: what it names must be in scope. The rules apply to links from a component's note and from any Markdown file it ships. Code is fully literal: nothing inside a code span or fenced block is read, so a call, link or embed written there ships exactly as written (rule 12). A plugin-root path, ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>, is not link syntax and is read in prose and code alike (rules 15 to 26).

comments.text: I wonder if we should error on malformed frontmatter, bc malformed frontmatter could lead to bad prose being transcluded right?

replies.text:
Agreed. With a broken frontmatter fence the body boundary is unknown:

1. Note starts `---`, YAML lines, but the closing `---` is missing.
2. Treat it all as body: the YAML gets inlined as prose.
3. Guess a boundary: real prose may get dropped.

Either way the shipped skill is wrong with no signal. So the rule becomes: embedding a note with malformed frontmatter (unclosed fence or invalid YAML) is an error naming both notes. Being applied in the current revision.
Done: embedding a note with malformed frontmatter is an error naming both notes. Section 6 and the appendix agree.
